chunks: From him, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (some) of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Musa (peace be upon him) said to Al-Khizr (peace be upon him): 'I have been sanctified by your company, so advise me.' He said to him: 'Adhere to that which, along with it, nothing will harm you, just as nothing will benefit you along with that which is other than it.'

key_terms.تَحَرَّمْتُ: I have been sanctified / made sacred
key_terms.لَا يَنْفَعُكَ مَعَ غَيْرِهِ شَيْءٌ: nothing will benefit you along with that which is other than it
key_terms.مَا لَا يَضُرُّكَ مَعَهُ شَيْءٌ: that which, along with it, nothing will harm you

ai.seo_question: What is the advice Musa received from Al-Khizr regarding the effect of faith on good and bad deeds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Musa (AS) seeks guidance from Al-Khizr (AS), who prescribes the preservation of *Iman* (faith) as the essential core that renders other deeds either beneficial or detrimental. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly principle that faith acts as the decisive filter for the acceptance of actions, aligning with the chapter's theme that evil deeds cannot harm the faithful, just as good deeds cannot save the disbeliever. The advice highlights the primacy of internal conviction over external ritual, a key concept in Usul al-Din.

en.hubeali: From him, from Yunus, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Musaas said to Al-Khizras: ‘You have sanctified meas by youras company, therefore advise meas’. Heas said to himas: ‘Necessitate (Emān) what would not harm youas anything along with it, just as it would not benefit youas anything along with other than it’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Yunus from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Moses said to Khidr, ‘I am honored to associate with you. Instruct me with good advice.’ Khidr said, ‘Hold fast to that with which nothing can harm you just as things without it will not benefit you.”’
